notes: A clean six-bullet page with one non-step and one merge. Bullet 1 is a precondition -- you must zone after Hearts of Mythril before Elki will offer this -- and not something you do at a place, so it is not a rung. Bullets 3 and 4 are merged: bullet 3 only says 'travel to the top floor of Palborough Mines', which is the same zone the toolbox is in, so a separate travel rung would point at the zone the very next rung already names, and its sub-bullet (Home Point #1) is route advice. The Old Toolbox is a real markable entity -- it resolves as an NPC key -- so this quest gets a marker on the object itself rather than only on a zone. The page writes the object 'Old Toolbox' and the key item 'Old toolbox'; both are recorded as written and both resolve. The Small Sword in the header is the reward and proves the quest is over, not that a step is done, so it is not evidence anywhere.

notes: A three-bullet Dominion Op: take it, kill the quota, report it. The trailing 'For more information, see Dominion Ops.' is a cross-reference and not a bullet at all. 'Dominion Sergeant' is a generic name the resolver marks ambiguous -- there are sergeants in every Abyssea zone -- so every step here carries Abyssea - Uleguerand explicitly; without the zone the whole quest would be demoted to start-only. Bullet 3 says ANY sergeant may be reported to, so the marker on step 3 is a convenience, not a constraint; the nearest one in the zone will do. The five kills are not observable -- no packet reports a kill count -- so the fight step carries no evidence and the ladder cannot tell 0 kills from 4. That is honest rather than fixable. The wiki writes the mob plural ('Mechanical Menaces'); the singular is what get_mob_list will show, so that is what is recorded.

notes:
Three bullets that are one interaction with one object. Bullet 1 selects the ???, bullet 2 is the menu choice inside that same conversation (its sub-bullet only warns that picking a type other than the equipped one needs that other weapon), and bullet 3 is the trade that finishes it. None of the three is markable -- the target is a bare ??? throughout -- and none is observable, so three rungs the player cannot be tracked through are noise and they collapse to one, with the order kept in the note.

The header names the giver 'Kupofried, (???) Walk of Echoes' -- it says outright that the entity is a ???. Start is recorded as Kupofried because that is the only name the page gives that can resolve at all; if the live entity is a bare ??? the marker simply never appears, which is no worse than today. The steps keep the ??? as written rather than borrowing the header's name for something the walkthrough never calls Kupofried.

Two things are recorded with a shrug. The weapon requirement is a genuine OR -- Paikea or a level 90~99 Hvergelmir -- and both resolve, so it is modelled as items plus items_alt; but the page says the weapon must be EQUIPPED, and holding is all that can be seen. And 'Level: 90~99' is the weapon's tier restated rather than a character level, so the gate is set at the bottom of that range, which cannot wrongly hide the quest from anyone who could actually do it. 'Guardian of the Void' arrives via Quest Reqs rather than Previous, but it is a quest name and belongs in prev. The reward is an ability, not an item, so there is nothing to observe at the end either.

steps.note: in order: select the ??? with the weapon EQUIPPED, choose the weapon type to unlock, then trade the weapon for the scene that unlocks Myrkr. The Hvergelmir must be level 90~99. Equipped, not merely held, is the real requirement and only holding is visible.

notes: A three-bullet fetch quest and all three bullets are steps. Bullet 2's sub-bullets are sourcing and routing advice -- the lumber drops from monsters on the Phanauet Channel barge or from ones that spawn while fishing on the barge or the pier, and the Survival Guide lands you at South Landing where the barge boards -- so they stay as a note. The middle step is an obtain with no target: the page names no vendor, no NPC and no ??? for the lumber, only a zone and a way of getting it, so inventing a hand-in there would be exactly the guessing to avoid. It carries the Garhada Teak Lumber as evidence, which is the one thing on this page that can actually be seen. The header's 'Quest Reqs: Gar. Teak Lumber Garhada Teak Lumber' is that same item restated -- short name then long name, run together by the renderer -- and not a prerequisite quest, so prev stays empty; both spellings resolve to the same item and the long one is used. 'Next: Hyper Active' is downstream information and gates nothing here.

notes:
Five bullets, and the page fights itself in the middle. Bullet 2 says to trade the Ripped Cap to Paytah; bullet 3 then says to trade the Ripped Cap to Baren-Moren. Both are kept, because the only reading under which the page is consistent is that Paytah hands the cap back -- he is a child minding his father's cap and the whole point is that he cannot fix it. Recorded as written, demoted to medium, and flagged rather than quietly dropping one of the two.

Bullet 2 is split: fishing the cap out of the water is an obtain and the only observable thing on this page, and trading it to Paytah is a separate action on a separate entity. Bullets 3 and 4 merge the other way -- both are Baren-Moren, one naming the cap and one naming the four hides -- so they are one trade with the full AND-list; the page does not say whether the game wants one trade or two, and the note says so.

The last step is deliberately thin. Bullet 5 calls it only 'the repaired cap' and never names the item, so nothing is recorded to hold; inventing a name for it would cost more than the empty list does. The Dhalmel Mantle and Leather Ring are the header's reward and prove the quest is over, not that a step is done, so neither is evidence. Baren-Moren is written 'Windurst Waters South', which is half of zone 238 and not a zone of its own, so the zone is Windurst Waters with the grid kept.
